rv.q: It is sweet, funny and surprisingly moving, even as it leans into its nostalgic weepie spirit.

DEAR JACK, DEAR LOUISE is a heartfelt, personal play, and its delightful performances by Feiler and Nyman will make audiences laugh, cry, and want to give their loved ones a hug — or indeed, send a letter.
Well, it turned out to be remarkably engaging, and oozing with refreshing optimism without descending into saccharine emotions and goopy melodrama.
Dear Jack, Dear Louise is a sweet story full of wit and goodness and a sense that everything will be alright in the end.
It’s both a loveable two-hander and a deeply satisfying true-romance.
That truth gives the play an added glow — a reminder that even in the bleakest moments of history, connection and love persist.
Refreshing, amusing and moving, 'Dear Jack, Dear Louise' brings hope and love to a world fractured by war where everything feels impossible.
The play is joyful and moving while never making light of the setting.

Although the germ of Dear Jack, Dear Louise exhibits aptitude, the script limits itself to an overly conventional execution, where a basic recipe is followed to the letter without any additional spices.

cn.t: Critics praise this charming WWII epistolary romance as sweet, witty, and uplifting. Ludwig's two-hander about pen pals falling in love through letters delights with authentic period detail, strong chemistry between leads, and heartfelt storytelling.
